acceptance: Weld business personal property (co.bpp.weld_declaration): preparing builds the January 1 snapshot from BookAsset records owned on that January 1 (placed in service on or before it, not disposed on or before it; the truck is never a BookAsset, so vehicles are excluded by construction). Each item carries its description (type, make, model, serial), year acquired, original cost and — when it was rented out on January 1 — the renter's name and address and its rental line from the assignment in force that day. Items over $350 are listed individually (the first-time-filer rule; first-time means no earlier BPP filing was ever submitted). The total original cost is compared with the dated co.bpp.exemption_threshold rule ($56,000 for 2026, seeded by this card's migration as a researched rule version): at or under, preparation ends with the filing in NOT_APPLICABLE, the numbers kept, saying 'No declaration needed'; over, the filing prepares normally. The comparison basis (original cost, which the assessor converts to actual value from cost and year) is stated on the filing itself.

Over the threshold, the filing downloads the filled DS 056 and DS 060 forms and the itemized spreadsheet (CSV) from the approved filing's snapshot only. Both PDFs are the official Weld County forms vendored into src/domains/compliance/forms/co/ and pinned in the forms manifest (DS 056 SHA-256 15575c69dfd98232c2a5569da98a84254fcb7f9fccdfe4bcc5d7e76418d1d5ce; DS 060 SHA-256 1b126326757d97c04fd9546d00ee8940803c73bb01cf49d87015017307ca8bc3), filled through the same manifest-checked engine as the earlier forms: business identity, the item rows the form has room for (the full listing always rides the spreadsheet, as the form itself instructs), and on DS 060 the renter name/address per unit and the monthly rent only when the unit is its rental line's only appliance — a set's rent is never split by invention; the line label and its whole monthly price ride the spreadsheet instead. The prepared section shows the extension choice near the due date with the fees from the dated co.bpp.extension rule ($20 for 10 days, $40 for 20, requested by April 15). The snapshot covers the appliance fleet the app tracks; tools and office equipment are not recorded anywhere in the app, so the filing says plainly that any must be added by hand — no rows are invented for them.

SOS periodic report (co.sos.periodic_report): preparation now shows the exact values to type on the Secretary of State site — the LLC's legal name, the principal office address (the CMP-3 payer identity), the registered agent's name and address (new Business facts), the report month, the filing window and the $25 fee — and the existing mark-filed flow captures the confirmation number.

Trade name (co.sos.trade_name): the renewal rule is now confirmed from the statute (C.R.S. § 7-71-104) — a trade name held by a reporting entity such as an LLC stays effective in perpetuity while the entity remains in good standing, so there is no renewal filing and no dates are invented. The obligation is handled at the obligation level, like every unscheduled CMP-1 entry: unrecorded, it sits in Needs you asking for the fact; once a trade name is recorded in Business facts it moves to Not needed, explaining that it stays effective while the LLC is in good standing (the periodic report is what keeps the standing) — no filing row, no dates, no invented renewal. DQ-CMP-TRADE-NAME is updated with the confirmed rule. This adapts the card's 'trade name as exact values to type' acceptance: there is no renewal form to type them into, and building one would be inventing a filing.

Greeley business license (greeley.business_license): the renewal cycle is wired from the recorded license date — a period every two years on that date, opening 60 days ahead, no fee (the city's business license page, researched 2026-10-27; the spec's starting value, with DQ-CMP-GREELEY updated and still the owner's to confirm). With no license date recorded the obligation stays unscheduled with that reason rather than a guessed date.

Vehicle and USDOT (co.vehicle_registration, fed.usdot): the truck registration obligation gains yearly periods in the recorded registration month (due the last day of that month) once the month is a Business fact. The USDOT obligation (only at GVWR 16,001 lb or more, unchanged) gains its biennial periods once the USDOT number is recorded: the last digit sets the filing month (1 = January … 9 = September, 0 = October) and the next-to-last digit sets odd or even years (the FMCSA schedule), due the last day of that month. No number recorded → no dates, with the reason shown.

Business facts gain the CMP-4 fields (trade name, USDOT number, truck registration month, Greeley license date, registered agent name and address), owner-only and audited by field name only, following the CMP-1 facts pattern; the compliance context and the filing sync use them, and the facts screen explains each in plain words.

Tests named by the work index pass: tests/bpp-snapshot.test.ts, tests/local-filings.test.ts, tests/colorado-local-integration.test.ts, tests/compliance-forms.test.ts (extended for the DS forms), tests/rules-registry.test.ts (the two new rule seeds); ci green; every review comment read.
invariants: No date is invented: Greeley, vehicle and USDOT periods exist only when the fact they derive from is recorded; the trade name gets no renewal dates because the confirmed rule has none.

No number is invented: the BPP threshold and extension fees come from dated rule versions read with ruleAsOf at the January 1 instant; a missing rule yields words, not a guessed threshold. A set's monthly rent is never split across its appliances by invention.

Nothing is filed by the app: CMP-4 prepares forms, values and spreadsheets inside the CMP-1 prepare → approve flow (preparedHash binding); filing happens on the county, SOS, city and FMCSA sites by the owner, and the confirmation is captured afterwards.

Money stays integer cents; times are stored UTC and shown America/Denver; the January 1 snapshot compares business dates, not raw timestamps; writes lock the row first and re-check the actor inside the transaction.

Prepared data holds no full tax id (the prepared-data guard is unchanged); renter names and addresses appear only inside the owner's own filing snapshot and its downloads, exactly what the lessor form itself requires.

outcome: Colorado and local filings work end to end: the Weld property declaration is built from the fleet's own records with the $56,000 exemption honestly applied (under → 'No declaration needed' with the numbers kept; over → filled DS 056/DS 060 forms plus the itemized spreadsheet and the extension choice); the SOS periodic report shows the exact values to type with confirmation capture; the trade name is handled by its confirmed rule (no renewal exists for an LLC); and the Greeley license, truck registration and USDOT update are scheduled from the owner's recorded facts — never from guessed dates.
